scope: Independent source-only review of v2 pending queue VecDeque design
verdict: Suitable to preserve as a proposed design; not an approved or qualified implementation and no measured performance result.
checks: Verified five v14 source files against pinned fixed-input catalog using the supplied verifier.
Verified v2 archive members, manifest hashes, exact nested v1 archive and retained v14 hosted job log.
Inspected Worker drain, account, sticky, cleanup and split ownership paths, pinned Tokio recv_many cancellation documentation, retained-backing test and hosted summary.
Confirmed N*(N-1)/2 is 8,386,560 logical shifted tail positions for 4096 fixed items drained singly; actual work and causal contribution remain unmeasured.
resolved_review_findings: Client enforces TCP_NODELAY while mock ignores setter errors; effective options unmeasured.
Back-popped selection reverses record order; success and cancellation require explicitly tracked forward/reverse orientation.
Receive chunk changes may alter batching, linger, backpressure and scheduling; sticky admission/cohort visibility and lock boundaries need explicit preservation.
Sticky singleton must stay owned across earliest-deadline refresh and rollback to the front on cancellation.
Synchronous large batch commit and Drop recovery remain potentially linear and can affect responsiveness.
Tokio 1.53.3 documents cancellation safety when another select branch wins; after successful receipt, scratch still needs durable worker ownership.
implementation_blockers: No actual implementation or behavioral proof; exact stage transitions, extraction/reversal and rollback under every cancellation and unwind boundary remain to be designed and tested.
A producer-wide record/object and framework-owned memory policy is not defined; a deque alone does not supply one.
The proposed bounded receive scratch must not silently change sticky cohort ordering, batch semantics or timer/expiry accounting.
Existing retained-backing and other client failures remain unresolved; hosted panic body is unavailable.
The benchmark must bind the eventual candidate and source, measure optimized code with equivalent workloads and validate real record outcomes; no benchmark has run.
limits: No Cargo, compiler, Rust tests, Kafka interoperability, benchmark, publication or production qualification was performed.
The review does not establish the cause of the hosted test failure or any performance gain.
The design is pinned to v14; later candidate source changes require rebinding and review.
